chunks: Saad ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazee', from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Hamid ibn Sa'id, from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who entered into the state of Ihram for Hajj on the Day of Tarwiyah from near the Maqam (Station of Abraham), then performed Tawaf around the House after entering Ihram, and he did not consider that this to be improper. I asked: Does his Tawaf around the House break his Ihram? He said: 'No, but he continues in his Ihram.'

And for the Mutamatti' (one who performs Umrah then Hajj), his Umrah is complete as long as he catches the two stations (Arafah and Muzdalifah). It makes no difference whether this is on the Day of Tarwiyah, or the Night of Arafah, or the Day of Arafah until after the sun has passed its zenith. When the sun passes its zenith on the Day of Arafah, the Mut'ah is missed because he will not be able to join the people at Arafah.

The situation remains as described, except that people's ranks differ in virtue and reward. Whoever catches the Day of Tarwiyah at the time of the sun's zenith will have greater reward and a more complete Mut'ah than one who joins on the night. And whoever joins on the night will have less reward than that, but more than one who joins on the Day of Arafah after the sun's zenith.

And the narrations that have come stating that whoever does not catch the Day of Tarwiyah has missed the Mut'ah, the meaning is the loss of the perfection which he hopes for by joining on the Day of Tarwiyah.

And what they included from their saying (peace be upon them): 'And let him make it an individual Hajj,' means that the person has the choice in this matter between continuing with the Mut'ah and making it an individual Hajj, provided he does not fear missing the two stations, and his Hajj is not the Hajj of Islam (the obligatory one) in which individual Hajj is not permissible when capable, as we have previously stated.

And the obligation and necessity of making it an individual Hajj applies only to one who is convinced that if he engages in Tawaf, Sa'i, and Ihlal (exiting Ihram), then re-entering Ihram for Hajj, he will miss the two stations.
And however we interpret these narrations according to what we mentioned, we have not rejected any of them.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: State of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.إِحْلَال: Exiting the state of Ihram after Umrah before Hajj
key_terms.الْمَوْقِفَانِ: The two stations of Arafah and Muzdalifah
key_terms.الْمُتَمَتِّعُ: One who performs Umrah then Hajj in the same season
key_terms.زَوَالُ الشَّمْسِ: The time when the sun passes its zenith (midday)
key_terms.يَوْمَ التَّرْوِيَةِ: The 8th of Dhu al-Hijjah, when pilgrims proceed to Mina

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on Tawaf breaking Ihram for Mutamatti' and how is the reward for Hajj determined by timing?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi clarifies that Tawaf does not invalidate Ihram and defines the validity of Umrat al-Tamattu' by the ability to reach Arafah before sunset, while establishing a hierarchy of spiritual merit for earlier arrival. The text resolves apparent contradictions in hadith regarding 'missing' the Mut'ah by distinguishing between the loss of optimal reward (kamaal) and the loss of validity, thereby permitting the choice between Tamattu' and Qiran (individual Hajj) provided the two stations are not missed. This reflects the Shia juristic principle of balancing textual evidence with practical feasibility for the pilgrim.
